title: M: The Third Measure
meter: Prose (the Upaniṣad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pāda and mātrā, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
devanagari: मिनोति ह वा इदं सर्वमपीतिश्च भवति य एवं वेद॥
iast: minoti ha vā idaṃ sarvam apītiś ca bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
translation: Prājña, whose field is deep sleep, is M, the third measure: because it measures (miti), or because all merges into it (apīti). Whoever knows this measures all this and becomes the place where all merges.
translation_hi: सुषुप्ति अवस्था वाला प्राज्ञ मकार है, तीसरी मात्रा, क्योंकि वह मापता है (मिति) या क्योंकि सब उसमें विलीन होता है (अपीति)। जो ऐसा जानता है वह इस सबको माप लेता है और सबका लय स्थान बन जाता है।
grammar: Root √mā 'measure' once more: मिति, मिनोति, मात्रा, and from earlier pages प्रमाण (measure), मेय (measurable), मान (amount). One root runs through mathematics, meter and the Upaniṣad.
M closes: Om ends with the lips closing on M; all sound 'merges' into it, as waking and dream merge into deep sleep.
